abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the expression profile of leptin and leptin receptors in gestational trophoblastic diseases (GTDs). METHODS: Using immunohistochemical staining on archival paraffin-embedded tissue sections, we studied the expression of leptin and leptin receptor in hydatidiform moles, with gestational age-matched normal first-trimester placenta used as control. A total of 38 cases of hydatidiform moles were studied, including 20 complete moles (CHMs) and 18 partial moles (PHMs). Among them, 10 cases of the CHM group and 8 cases of the PHM group subsequently developed residual trophoblastic disease (RTD). In addition, two cases of choriocarcinoma and three cases of placental site trophoblastic tumor (PSTT) were also studied. Reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) was further performed using RNA extracted from frozen tissue (five CHMs, four PHMs and nine normal first-trimester placenta) to study the expression of leptin and individual leptin receptor isoforms at the transcription level. RESULTS: In all tissue sections, immunostaining signal was shown in the cytoplasmic compartment of cytotrophoblasts and syncytiotrophoblasts, with much stronger staining in the former. Significantly higher immunostaining intensity was shown for both leptin (P < 0.05) and leptin receptor (P < 0.001) in both CHMs and PHMs compared to normal first-trimester placenta. There was no significant difference between those cases subsequently developing RTD and those which did not (P > 0.05). In the choriocarcinoma and PSTT cases, intense immunostaining was found in the tumor cells. RT-PCR revealed that the expression of leptin and all leptin receptor isoforms were significantly higher in both CHMs and PHMs than in normal placenta (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: There is up-regulated expression of leptin and leptin receptor in GTDs. However, there is no obvious correlation with the development of RTD. The exact role played by leptin and its receptors in the pathogenesis of GTDs awaits further investigations.
abstract_ja: 目的:妊娠性絨毛性疾患(GTD)におけるレプチンおよびレプチン受容体の発現プロファイルを調べる。方法:保存パラフィン包埋組織切片を用いた免疫組織化学染色により、胞状奇胎におけるレプチンおよびレプチン受容体の発現を検討した。対照として妊娠週数をマッチさせた正常妊娠初期胎盤を用いた。胞状奇胎は計38例で、完全胞状奇胎(CHM)20例と部分胞状奇胎(PHM)18例を含んだ。このうちCHM群の10例とPHM群の8例は、その後残存絨毛性疾患(RTD)を発症した。さらに絨毛癌2例と胎盤部トロホブラスト腫瘍(PSTT)3例も検討した。凍結組織から抽出したRNAを用いた逆転写ポリメラーゼ連鎖反応(RT-PCR)を追加し、レプチンおよび個々のレプチン受容体アイソフォームの転写レベルの発現を検討した(CHM5例、PHM4例、正常初期胎盤9例)。結果:すべての組織切片において、免疫染色シグナルは細胞性栄養膜細胞および合胞体栄養膜細胞の細胞質に認められ、前者でより強い染色を示した。CHMおよびPHMは、正常初期胎盤と比較して、レプチン(P<0.05)およびレプチン受容体(P<0.001)の両方で有意に高い免疫染色強度を示した。その後RTDを発症した症例と発症しなかった症例の間に有意差は認められなかった(P>0.05)。絨毛癌およびPSTT症例では、腫瘍細胞に強い免疫染色シグナルが認められた。RT-PCRでは、レプチンおよびすべてのレプチン受容体アイソフォームの発現は、正常胎盤と比較してCHMおよびPHMで有意に高かった(P<0.05)。結論:GTDではレプチンおよびレプチン受容体の発現が上昇している。しかし、RTDの発生との明らかな相関は認められなかった。GTDの病態形成におけるレプチンおよびその受容体の正確な役割は、さらなる研究を待つ必要がある。
